projects.name: ECC Salesforce Case Management App
projects.description: A Salesforce Lightning case management app (ECC Manager) built for a Washington nonprofit, now headed to the Salesforce AppExchange. An Apex service layer aggregates case records by pipeline stage — Initiation through Closed — and feeds a custom LWC System Health dashboard: a Pipeline Overview funnel, a Bottleneck View that flags cases stalled past their expected case age, and Data Quality Flags for missing or invalid fields. Record-triggered Flows and Approval Processes route cases needing supervisor sign-off and keep case status updated automatically.

projects.description: A full-stack AI fashion platform: users build a digital wardrobe and get AI-generated outfit recommendations from their saved garments. Placed 3rd out of 10+ teams at a hackathon.

caseStudy.label: The hackathon
caseStudy.title: Third of 10+ teams.
caseStudy.body: Fabriq started at a hackathon. I led a team of four and built across the whole stack: the frontend, the backend, the API and the database, plus keeping each user's state straight across the app. We placed 3rd in a track of more than ten teams.

caseStudy.label: The problem
caseStudy.title: You forget what you own.
caseStudy.body: Clothes get buried in the closet, you buy something you already have, and getting dressed takes longer than it should. Fabriq keeps your whole wardrobe in one place: add a photo of each piece, sort it by category, and save the outfits you like.

caseStudy.label: How it picks an outfit
caseStudy.title: From a photo to your own clothes.
stages: You upload an outfit you like
The AI describes its top, bottom and shoes
A second pass picks matches from your closet
The code checks it's one top, one bottom, one pair of shoes
exits: A fallback outfit from your closet
caseStudy.note: Both AI steps use OpenAI's GPT-4o mini, and they run in a Vercel serverless function, so the API key never reaches the browser. If the model's answer comes back broken or incomplete, the code fills the gaps from your wardrobe instead of showing an error.

projects.name: Quantum Computing Research
projects.description: Quantum computing is a developing technology that has the potential to change several aspects of computing as we know it. In this paper, we introduce several essential components of quantum computing such as qubits, superposition, and entanglement. In addition, we discuss two examples of quantum computing: quantum teleportation and Grover's Algorithm. Our coverage of quantum teleportation provides an example of a property of quantum computing that is impossible using classical computing. In addition to this property, we cover Grover's Algorithm which is a key advancement in quantum computing, providing quadratic speedup for unstructured search problems compared to classical algorithms. We explain the algorithm's principles, including amplitude amplification and the role of the oracle. Our findings underscore the significant potential of quantum computing in solving complex problems more efficiently than classical methods.
projects.summary: An introduction to qubits, superposition, and entanglement, walking through quantum teleportation and Grover's Algorithm and its quadratic speedup for unstructured search.
projects.role: Co-author (with Malaya Jove; advised by Dr. Ryan Card)

projects.name: NASA GRACE Climate Data Science Research
projects.description: This study uses statistical and machine learning techniques to impute missing data from GRACE (Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment) terrestrial water storage (TWS) datasets. We examined information from 2 of the 62 watersheds across the globe, taking into account variables such as temperature, precipitation, evapotranspiration, NDVI, and ENSO. Creating models to predict TWS and efficiently impute missing values was our aim. We investigated techniques including Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Deep Neural Networks (DNN), Generalized Linear Models (GLM), and mean/median imputation. Mean Squared Error (MSE) was used to assess these models' performance to choose the most effective method for precise forecasting and imputation.
projects.summary: Using XGBoost, deep neural networks, and GLMs to predict and impute missing NASA GRACE terrestrial water storage data from climate variables across two global watersheds.
projects.role: Co-author (with Jenna Weldon; advised by Tamer Elbayoumi, mentored by Brett Hunter)

chapters.label: where it almost stopped

chapters.line: I wanted to study computer science. My GPA said otherwise, and advisors told me to pick something else.

chapters.label: where it changed

chapters.line: I didn't switch. I retook the prerequisites, fell in love with math along the way, and came out with two majors: Computer Science and Mathematics at the University of Washington. 3.6 GPA, Dean's List, class of 2026.
